title: Registry isolation allowed programmatic iframe creation outside the static sandbox check

examples: document.createElement('iframe') followed by setAttribute('sandbox', ...) and src assignment
const create = document.createElement; create('iframe') followed by sandbox/src property assignment
reproduction.beforeFix: The gate returned pass for programmatic iframe creation, including cases that set sandbox after creation and cases using aliased or namespace-aware factories.
reproduction.afterFix: The gate rejects iframe elements created by registry code because it cannot prove that sandbox attributes and navigation lifecycle remain safe across later mutations.

rootCause: The isolation rule validated statically authored JSX iframe attributes but did not track the lifecycle of iframe nodes assembled through DOM APIs.
remediation: Reject programmatically created iframe elements from registry resources, including direct, aliased, and createElementNS forms. Keep iframe previewing in the separately controlled opaque-origin preview host.

validation.redBeforeFix: pnpm exec vitest run packages/registry-gate/src/__tests__/registry-gate.test.ts -t "programmatically created iframe elements"
validation.redBeforeFixResult: failed as expected: all tested programmatic iframe forms returned pass before the fix
validation.canonicalResourceReview: No canonical resource contains a programmatically created iframe; a text-only description references iframe preview isolation.

runtimeBoundary: This is a static admission-control finding for untrusted registry source. Canonical resources do not rely on DOM-created iframes. The opaque-origin preview remains the supported iframe boundary; deployed verification remains pending.
